newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Holocaust fund to help east European Jews.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Holocaust fund to help east European Jews.

text.p: Switzerland's Holocaust memorial fund will make a first payment of 17 million Swiss francs ($11.6 million) to Jewish Holocaust survivors, primarily in eastern Europe, Swiss radio reported on Monday.
The panel's seven-member executive board made the decision at its inaugural meeting in Berne, the radio said. A government official confirmed the report.

"We can be satisfied because we have sent a signal that we are serious about helping, that things are moving forward, and that we can provide initial assistance to these primarily elderly people," panel chairman Rolf Bloch told the radio.

Panel members had cited the special plight of Holocaust survivors in eastern Europe, known as "double victims" for their inbility to get compensation during the Cold War for their suffering during Hitler's systematic murder of six million Jews and many others deemed unworthy to live.

The Swiss memorial fund administers some 170 million Swiss francs in donations from commercial banks and other private busineses eager to burnish Switzerland's humanitarian image amid charges the country cynically profited from World War Two.
The Swiss National Bank plans to add another 100 million if parliament approves and the plan is not shot down by voters in a referendum that opponents could force.
